text:
Mia (PM): quick sync—customer ACME wants a private deploy path that preserves their existing IP addresses and requires zero public-facing nodes. want to map expectations before we scope the next sprint.

Ryan (Eng): noted. is this for the new slim-installer or the full distro?

Mia (PM): they prefer slim-installer but will accept a small agent if it means no changes to their NAT/BGP. main ask: installer must be able to run entirely behind customer NAT, no inbound ports.

Leo (NetOps): behind-nat-only is possible, but we need an outbound tunnel/orchestrator. two options: persistent reverse-tunnel to a customer-controlled relay, or ephemeral egress to a redwood relay in customer's VPC.

Olivia (Field): customer legal won't allow redwood-hosted relays in their account. they'd run a relay in their VPC. we should support a "relay URL" param in the installer.

Ryan (Eng): ok. so installer needs to accept RELAY_HOST, RELAY_TOKEN, and create an mTLS connection outbound. fallback behavior?

Mia (PM): fallback = block install + clear error + support link. no silent fallbacks.

Adrian (SRE): operational concerns: this relay pattern affects metrics and tracing. we need a route for logs/health to go to their S3/Kinesis or to our agent-forwarder. define retention and RBAC.

Ryan (Eng): proposal: implement a thin agent that tunnels gRPC over a single outbound connection with mTLS. config file:
```
relay: 
  host: ${RELAY_HOST} 
  port: 443
  mtls_cert_path: /etc/redwood/mtls.pem
  token: ${RELAY_TOKEN}
```

Leo (NetOps): add note to docs about IP ranges egress must allow. customer NAT pools often rotate — advise a small egress CIDR list and provide a health-check endpoint for validation.

Olivia (Field): dev note — customers will ask for deterministic upgrade windows. can we support staged upgrade using agent checks and explicit approval?

Ryan (Eng): we can implement an upgrade orchestration protocol: agent reports current version and accepts a signed upgrade manifest. keep it offline-friendly.

Mia (PM): launch criteria suggestion: 1) installer can deploy behind NAT with only outbound 443 egress; 2) relay config works with customer-hosted relay; 3) upgrade manifest + staged rollout support; 4) docs + 2 field pilot customers; 5) automated health-check script.

Adrian (SRE): add SLA note: if customer relay drops, agent must backoff with jitter and alert customer admin. no auto-failover to hosted relays.

Leo (NetOps): question: how do we handle customer IP preservation for peering and egress? we must support SNAT-preserve and BGP advertisement in their environment—documented as "operator task" not automated.

Olivia (Field): customers will also request a non-root installer mode for security teams. this increases complexity (capabilities with systemd socket activation etc.).

Ryan (Eng): track as engineering debt: non-root mode + airgapped assets. for sprint 1 we target root install only, with clear customer-facing limitations.

Mia (PM): prioritization: Must-have for Q2 field pilots: behind-NAT install, relay param, signed upgrade manifests, health-check. Nice-to-have: non-root, installer GUI, and automated BGP helper.

Olivia (Field): tag tickets: FIELD-312 (pilot 1), FIELD-313 (pilot 2), and include runbook for netops with checklist.

Adrian (SRE): can we add a quick acceptance test script that customers run and paste output into the support form? something like `./redwood-check --relay ${RELAY_HOST}`

Ryan (Eng): yes — add `redwood-check` that validates TLS, token auth, and semantic version handshake. we'll include sample output in docs.

Mia (PM): next steps: Ryan + Leo draft an initial design doc by EOD Wednesday, Olivia to line up two pilot customers, Adrian to outline SRE runbook, I'll consolidate launch criteria and backlog tickets.

deploybot: Reminder: draft design doc due in 72 hours — create PR referencing RFC-5912 and FIELD tickets.

Olivia (Field): FYI I'll ping ACME legal to confirm relay-in-vpc acceptance today.

Ryan (Eng): ack, starting a design doc branch: <https://redwood.internal/docs/r/priv-deploy-relay-design> :eyes:

Mia (PM): perfect — thanks all. we'll reconvene after doc review. :thumbsup:
